Privacy policy

Last updated: 24 November 2026

We don’t track you. There’s no account, no ads and no analytics, and the app contains no tracking or crash-reporting code. This page explains what the app keeps on your phone and the few things that leave it.

What stays on your phone

Your notes, likes, bookmarks, reading plans, reading progress, streak, Community vote and settings are stored in the app on this phone. We can’t see them.

What leaves your phone

Content downloads: when the app downloads studies, devotionals, the Discover and Community lists, the donation history or ministry pictures, it requests files from our content server and our file storage, which Google hosts (Firebase Hosting and Firebase Storage). The requests contain no account or device ID, but like any internet request they show your IP address to Google.

Community vote: if you vote, the app sends “+1 for this ministry this month” to a counter hosted by Google (Cloud Firestore). It carries no account or device ID, and the counter stores only a number, but Google sees your IP address with the request. Checking whether voting is open works the same way. The app never shows vote counts. Your own choice stays on your phone.

Emails you choose to send: Report a problem and Send feedback open your own email app with a message you can read and change first. Nothing is sent unless you send it. If you do, we see your email address and what you wrote, and we may use it to correct the content.

Links you open: a ministry’s Website and Give directly buttons open its page in your browser. That site’s own privacy policy applies. The app handles no money.

What Android and Google Play do

If backup is turned on in your phone’s settings, Android may save a copy of your notes, plans and settings to your own Google account. On Android 12 and later, the app allows this only when Android can encrypt the backup end to end, which needs a screen lock. If you use Export my data, the file goes wherever you save it.

If you let your phone share usage and diagnostics with Google, Google Play may send us crash statistics. The app has no crash-reporting code of its own.

Who we share data with

We don’t sell personal information, we don’t share it for advertising, and nobody else gets data from the app. Google runs our content server and vote counter for us as a service provider, and sees IP addresses as described above. Google’s privacy policy (policies.google.com/privacy) covers that.

Keeping data safe

Everything the app downloads or sends goes over an encrypted connection (HTTPS), and the app refuses unencrypted ones. Downloaded files are checked against a published fingerprint before they’re used. Your notes and other data stay in the app’s private storage, which other apps can’t read.

How long data is kept

Data on your phone stays until you delete it or uninstall the app. The vote counter keeps only a total per ministry per month. Google keeps its server logs, which include IP addresses, for a limited time under its own policies, and we don’t use them to identify anyone. We keep emails you send only as long as we need them to answer you or correct the content, and we delete them sooner if you ask.

Deleting your data

Uninstalling the app, or clearing its data, deletes everything it stored on this phone. A backup in your Google account follows your Google account settings. Community votes can’t be deleted because they aren’t linked to anyone. To ask us to delete an email you sent, write to us.

Your rights

Depending on where you live (for example under the GDPR in the EU and UK, or the CCPA in California), you can ask to see, correct or delete personal data we hold about you, object to how we use it, and complain to your data protection authority. We have no account or profile for you, so the only personal data we might hold is an email you sent us. Write to us and we’ll answer within 30 days.

We use your email only to answer it and correct the content, because you chose to send it. IP addresses are needed for any download or vote to work, which is our legitimate interest in running the app.

Children

The app is for a general audience. It doesn’t ask anyone, including children, for personal information. If you think a child has emailed us personal information, write to us and we’ll delete it.
